tests.title: A valid create writes a pending workspace with every setting at its effective value
given: a signed-in user with a personal organization
a body naming a slug, a git URL and two settings
tests.when: POST /api/v1/workspaces is called and the workspace is then read back
then: the create answers 201 with status pending and access owner
display_name defaults to the slug and description to the empty string
the settings object carries all twelve keys, the two named at their given values and the rest at their defaults
the read returns the same record
tests.pseudocode: in the workspace routes' integration test file: r = post('/api/v1/workspaces', body); assert r.status == 201 and r.json.status == 'pending' and r.json.access == 'owner' and len(r.json.settings) == 12

tests.title: The slug rules accept exactly the documented shapes
given: a valid create body
tests.when: the slug is set to a 3-character minimum, a 64-character maximum, one of 2 and one of 65 characters, one starting with a digit or a hyphen, one ending with a hyphen, one with an uppercase letter, one with an underscore, one with two consecutive hyphens, and one already in use
then: the minimum, the maximum and an ordinary slug are accepted
every rule-breaking slug answers 400 and writes nothing
the slug already in use answers 409
tests.pseudocode: in the workspace validation test file, table over the slug cases asserting the status and that no row was written for a refusal

tests.title: A malformed create body is refused and writes nothing
given: a valid create body to vary
tests.when: slug or git_url is missing or malformed, display_name is 129 characters, description is 1025 characters, and workspace_mode, upstream_url and integration_branch are combined invalidly
then: each answers 400 naming the offending field
no workspace row and no secret is written for any of them
a carry_patch body with an upstream_url is accepted
tests.pseudocode: in the workspace validation test file, table over the malformed bodies asserting 400 and an unchanged store

tests.title: Invalid credential flag combinations are refused
given: a valid create body to vary
tests.when: git_pat is given with git_username, git_username is given without git_password, a credential value is empty, and a credential is given with an ssh git_url
then: each answers 400
no workspace row and no secret is written
git_pat alone with an https URL, and the full basic pair with an https URL, are both accepted
tests.pseudocode: in the workspace validation test file, table over the credential combinations

tests.title: The owning organization is resolved, or the create is refused
given: a user with a personal organization, a user with none, and an organization the first user does not belong to
tests.when: creates are made with no org_id, with an org_id naming nothing, with the foreign organization, and by the user with no personal organization and no org_id
then: the create with no org_id uses the caller's personal organization
an org_id naming nothing answers 400
the foreign organization answers 403
the user with no personal organization answers 400
tests.pseudocode: in the workspace routes' integration test file, table over the four cases asserting the status and the resulting org_id

tests.title: An admin token, an unscoped PAT and a duplicate slug are refused
given: an admin token, a PAT without workspaces:write, a PAT with it, and an existing workspace
tests.when: each credential creates a workspace, and the scoped PAT then repeats an existing slug
then: the admin token answers 403
the PAT without the scope answers 403, not 404
the duplicate slug answers 409
the scoped PAT's fresh slug succeeds
tests.pseudocode: in the workspace routes' test file, table over (credential, slug, expected)

tests.title: Creation credentials are stored as encrypted workspace secrets
given: a create body carrying a distinctive git_pat, and a second carrying a distinctive basic pair
tests.when: each workspace is created and the secret store's raw contents are inspected
then: GIT_PAT exists in the first workspace's scope and GIT_USERNAME and GIT_PASSWORD in the second's
the raw stored bytes contain neither distinctive value
no field of either create response carries the value
tests.pseudocode: in the workspace secrets integration test file: post(body with git_pat='SENTINEL9f3a'); assert 'GIT_PAT' in secret_names(ws); assert b'SENTINEL9f3a' not in raw_store_dump()

tests.title: The workspace list is scoped, ordered and filtered by include_archived
given: an owner with three workspaces, two created in the same instant, one of them archived, and one workspace of an unrelated user
tests.when: the list is requested with and without include_archived
then: the unrelated user's workspace never appears
the order is created_at descending, then slug ascending for the tie
the archived workspace is absent by default and present with include_archived=true
tests.pseudocode: in the workspace routes' integration test file: assert [w.slug for w in get('/api/v1/workspaces').json] == expectedOrder; assert archived in slugs(get('?include_archived=true'))

tests.title: One workspace is read by slug
given: a workspace owned by the caller
tests.when: GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug is requested
then: the response is 200 with the workspace
its slug matches the one requested
tests.pseudocode: in the workspace routes' test file: r = get(f'/api/v1/workspaces/{slug}'); assert r.status == 200 and r.json.slug == slug

tests.title: Every workspace object carries the full schema, with hub_url null where the reference says so
given: a service with an external URL configured and one without
a workspace with an organization and one without
tests.when: each workspace is read under each configuration
then: every response carries the documented keys and no others
display_name is never null or empty and description is never null
hub_url is the git server URL only when an external URL is configured and the workspace has an organization, and null otherwise
tests.pseudocode: in the workspace serialisation test file, table over (externalUrl, hasOrg, expectedHubUrl)

tests.title: The access field describes the caller and a member sees the owner's view
given: a workspace, its owner, a member of its organization and an admin token
tests.when: each reads the workspace and the workspace list
then: the owner sees access owner, the member access member and the admin token access admin
the member's object is field-for-field equal to the owner's except for access
the admin token's list carries every workspace
tests.pseudocode: in the workspace access integration test file: o = read(owner); m = read(member); assert m.json == {**o.json, 'access': 'member'}

tests.title: An update changes only the fields it names, and null restores a default
given: a workspace with a display name, a description and a non-default setting
tests.when: display_name alone is changed, then description is set to null, then display_name is set to null
then: each call answers 200
a field the body did not name is unchanged after every call
a null display_name returns it to the slug and a null description to the empty string
tests.pseudocode: in the workspace routes' integration test file, a sequence asserting each field after each call

tests.title: Setting the settings object to null returns every setting to its default
given: a workspace with four settings away from their defaults
tests.when: PATCH is called with settings set to null
then: the response is 200
all twelve keys read their documented defaults
tests.pseudocode: in the workspace settings test file: r = patch({'settings': None}); assert r.json.settings == DEFAULTS

tests.title: An empty, archived or immutable-field update is refused
given: an active workspace and an archived one
tests.when: PATCH is called with an empty body, on the archived workspace, with a 129-character display_name, with each immutable field, with sync_mode, and with an org_id naming nothing
then: each answers 400
the stored workspace is unchanged after every call
the immutable fields refused are slug, git_url, branch, owner_id, workspace_mode, upstream_url and integration_branch
tests.pseudocode: in the workspace routes' test file, table over the refused bodies asserting 400 and an unchanged record

tests.title: Moving a workspace to an organization its owner does not belong to is refused
given: a workspace and an organization its owner is not a member of
tests.when: PATCH sets org_id to that organization
then: the response is 403
the workspace's org_id is unchanged
tests.pseudocode: in the workspace routes' test file: r = patch({'org_id': foreign}); assert r.status == 403 and read().json.org_id == before

tests.title: A ready workspace is archived and its bound tokens survive
given: a ready workspace with a free lock and one live bound token
tests.when: the archive route is called
then: the response is 200 with status archived
the bound token is still live afterwards
a read of the workspace still returns it
tests.pseudocode: in the workspace lifecycle integration test file: assert post(archive).json.status == 'archived'; assert call(boundToken).status != 401

tests.title: Archiving is refused for an archived, cloning or busy workspace
given: an archived workspace, a cloning workspace and a ready workspace whose lock is held
tests.when: the archive route is called for each
then: the archived workspace answers 400
the cloning workspace answers 409
the busy workspace answers 409 with error_type workspace_busy
no status changes
tests.pseudocode: in the workspace lifecycle test file, table over the three cases asserting status, error_type and an unchanged record

tests.title: An archived workspace is reactivated to pending
given: an archived workspace
tests.when: the reactivate route is called
then: the response is 200 with status pending
a subsequent read reports pending
tests.pseudocode: in the workspace lifecycle integration test file: assert post(reactivate).json.status == 'pending'

tests.title: Reactivating a workspace that is not archived is refused
given: a ready workspace, a pending workspace and a failed workspace
tests.when: the reactivate route is called for each
then: each answers 409
no status changes
tests.pseudocode: in the workspace lifecycle test file, table over the three statuses asserting 409

tests.title: Deleting an archived workspace revokes its bound tokens in the same transaction
given: an archived workspace with two live bound tokens and one already-revoked bound token
tests.when: the delete route is called, and once more against a store that fails mid-transaction
then: the successful delete answers 204 and the workspace is gone from the list
both live tokens are refused 401 afterwards
when the store fails mid-transaction the workspace still exists and the tokens still work, so the two effects never diverge
tests.pseudocode: in the workspace lifecycle integration test file: delete(ws); assert call(t1).status == 401 and call(t2).status == 401; then with a failing store assert the workspace and tokens are both intact

tests.title: Deleting a workspace that is not archived is refused
given: a ready workspace with a live bound token
tests.when: the delete route is called
then: the response is 409
the workspace still exists
the bound token still works
tests.pseudocode: in the workspace lifecycle test file: assert delete(ws).status == 409 and read(ws).status == 200

tests.title: The twelve settings exist with their defaults and accept exactly their documented values
given: a freshly created workspace
tests.when: its settings are read, and each setting is set in turn to every value the reference lists for it
then: the settings object has exactly the twelve documented keys
each key's initial value is its documented default
every listed value is accepted for its key
tests.pseudocode: in the workspace settings test file, driven from a table of (key, default, allowedValues) transcribed from the reference

tests.title: A setting is set, reset to its default, or kept
given: a workspace with rebuild_strategy set to merge and sync_enabled set to false
tests.when: an update names rebuild_strategy with a value, gives sync_enabled as null, and names no other setting
then: rebuild_strategy holds the new value
sync_enabled holds its default
every setting the body did not name is unchanged
tests.pseudocode: in the workspace settings test file: r = patch({'settings': {'rebuild_strategy': 'rebase', 'sync_enabled': None}}); assert r.json.settings matches the three expectations

tests.title: An unknown setting key or an unacceptable value is refused
given: a workspace with known settings
tests.when: an update names a key that does not exist, gives an enum setting a value outside its list, and gives a boolean setting a string
then: each answers 400 naming the key
a bad enum value's message names the values the key accepts
no setting of the workspace changes, including ones named in the same body that were valid
tests.pseudocode: in the workspace settings test file, table over the bad settings bodies asserting 400 and an unchanged settings object

tests.title: One decision function yields the same level for a caller on every route
given: a workspace, its owner, a member, a stranger and an admin token
tests.when: the access level is computed for each caller through the routes of each access level
then: the owner is owner, the member is member, the admin token is admin and the stranger has none
the level for one caller and workspace is the same whichever route asked
tests.pseudocode: in the access decision's test file, table over (caller, routeLevel) asserting one decision function's output

tests.title: Membership is read on every request, so a removal takes effect at once
given: a workspace and a member of its organization holding a live credential
tests.when: the member reads the workspace, is removed from the organization, and reads it again with the same credential
then: the first read succeeds
the second is refused 404
no re-authentication, token refresh or restart happened in between
tests.pseudocode: in the access integration test file: assert read(member).status == 200; remove_member(); assert read(member).status == 404

tests.title: A member's read-level answer equals the owner's
given: a workspace, its owner and a member of its organization
tests.when: both call each read-level workspace route
then: the statuses are identical
the bodies are identical except for the access field
tests.pseudocode: in the access integration test file, table over the read-level routes comparing the two responses

tests.title: A member's write is refused with the documented message
given: a workspace and a member of its organization
tests.when: the member calls each write-level workspace route
then: each answers 403 with error_type forbidden
each message is "org members have read-only access to this workspace"
nothing is written
tests.pseudocode: in the access test file, table over the write-level routes asserting the status, error_type and message

tests.title: A private route is indistinguishable from a workspace that does not exist
given: a workspace, a member of its organization, a stranger, and a slug naming nothing
tests.when: the member and the stranger call a private-level route, and anyone calls any route for the unknown slug
then: every call answers 404 with the message "workspace not found"
the three responses are byte-for-byte identical
tests.pseudocode: in the access test file: assert resp(member) == resp(stranger) == resp(unknownSlug) and status == 404

tests.title: The checks run in the documented order
given: an archived workspace, a member of its organization, and a PAT without the route's scope held by that member
tests.when: the member writes to the archived workspace with a scoped credential, and then with the unscoped PAT
then: the scoped member's write answers 403 forbidden, not the 400 the archived status would give
the unscoped PAT gets the scope answer whatever its membership
a request with no credential gets 401 before either
tests.pseudocode: in the access test file, table over (credential, membership, workspaceStatus, expectedStatus, expectedErrorType)

tests.title: A failed access lookup refuses rather than grants
given: a store whose membership lookup raises
a recording route handler
tests.when: the owner, a member and a stranger each call a read-level and a write-level route
then: every call answers 500
the route handler is not invoked for any of them
no call is granted any access level
tests.pseudocode: in the access test file: with store.membership raising, assert every call's status == 500 and handler.calls == 0

tests.title: The six CRUD routes hide a missing scope behind 404, and every other route shows 403
given: a workspace and a PAT holding no workspace scope
tests.when: the PAT calls the workspace list, read, update and delete, the archive and reactivate routes, POST /api/v1/workspaces, and a representative non-CRUD workspace route
then: the six CRUD routes answer 404 with the message "workspace not found"
that answer is identical to the one for a slug naming nothing
POST /api/v1/workspaces and the non-CRUD route answer 403 with no error_type
tests.pseudocode: in the access test file, table over (route, expectedStatus) with the six anti-enumeration routes separated from the rest

tests.title: An owner mints a bound token that reaches its workspace
given: a workspace and its owner
tests.when: the bound-token route is called with a name, two scopes and an expiry, and the returned token is then used on its own workspace
then: the response is 201 with Cache-Control no-store, carrying the token, the workspace and the documented fields
the token is accepted on its own workspace under its scopes
no later route returns the token string
tests.pseudocode: in the bound token integration test file: r = post(f'/api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/tokens', body); assert r.headers['Cache-Control'] == 'no-store' and r.json.workspace == slug; assert read(slug, r.json.token).status == 200

tests.title: Only the owner may mint a bound token
given: a workspace, its owner, a member, a stranger, an admin token, an existing bound token, and an archived workspace
tests.when: each calls the bound-token mint route
then: the bound caller answers 403 with error_type token_bound
the admin token answers 403
the member and the stranger answer 404
the archived workspace answers 400
no token is created and no binding is written in any refused case
tests.pseudocode: in the bound token test file, table over (caller, workspaceStatus, expectedStatus, expectedErrorType)

tests.title: A workspace's bound tokens are listed, dead ones included and secrets never
given: an archived workspace with one live, one revoked and one expired bound token, plus a binding whose token has been deleted
tests.when: the owner and an admin token each list the workspace's tokens
then: the response is 200 with the live, revoked and expired tokens, ordered by created_at then token_id
the binding whose token is gone is left out
no entry carries a token string or a hash
the route works although the workspace is archived
tests.pseudocode: in the bound token integration test file: r = get(f'/api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/tokens'); assert ids(r.json) == expectedOrder and all('token' not in e for e in r.json)

tests.title: A bound token on another workspace's route is refused before any other check
given: a token bound to workspace S, another workspace T, an archived workspace, and a slug naming nothing
tests.when: the token calls routes naming T, the archived workspace and the unknown slug, including routes whose scope it does not hold
then: every call answers 404 with the message "workspace not found"
the three answers are identical, so the existence and status of the named workspace are not disclosed
the answer is 404 even where a missing scope would otherwise give 403
tests.pseudocode: in the bound token test file, table over the target workspaces and routes asserting an identical 404

tests.title: A bound token is refused with the right message on each kind of route it may not use
given: a token bound to workspace S
tests.when: it calls POST /api/v1/workspaces, a user-scoped secrets route, GET /api/v1/sandboxes, an unmatched path under the mount point, and an identity route
then: each answers 403 with error_type token_bound
the hub routes' message is "this token is bound to workspace S"
the identity route's message is "this token is bound to a workspace" and does not name it
tests.pseudocode: in the bound token test file, table over (route, expectedMessage)

tests.title: The sweep retires bindings whose workspace or token is gone and keeps the rest
given: a binding whose workspace was removed outside the delete route, a binding whose token was deleted, and a binding of a revoked token whose workspace still exists
tests.when: the sweep runs
then: the token of the removed workspace is revoked and its binding gone
the binding whose token is gone is removed
the revoked token's binding of the existing workspace is kept and still appears in that workspace's token list
tests.pseudocode: in the bound token integration test file: run_sweep(); assert call(orphanToken).status == 401 and binding(orphanToken) is None and binding(revokedButLive) is not None

tests.title: An unreadable binding refuses the request rather than treating the token as unbound
given: a store whose binding lookup raises, and a PAT that is in fact bound
tests.when: that token calls its own workspace's route, another workspace's route and a route no bound token may use
then: every call answers 500
no call is served as though the token were unbound
the route handler is not invoked
tests.pseudocode: in the bound token test file: with store.binding raising, assert every call's status == 500 and handler.calls == 0

tests.title: Two lock-taking operations on one workspace are serialised
given: a workspace and two lock-taking operations that record their start and end instants
a second workspace
tests.when: both operations are started concurrently on the first workspace, and then one on each workspace
then: on one workspace the two intervals do not overlap
on two different workspaces the intervals may overlap
both operations complete
tests.pseudocode: in the workspace lock integration test file: run concurrently and assert not overlapping(a, b) for one workspace, and allow overlap across workspaces

tests.title: A busy workspace refuses at once rather than waiting
given: a workspace whose lock is held by a long-running operation
a fixed clock to measure the wait
tests.when: a second lock-taking request is made, and then repeated after the lock is released
then: the second answers 409 with error_type workspace_busy
it answers without waiting for the lock to free
the repeat after release succeeds
tests.pseudocode: in the workspace lock test file: hold(lock); t0 = now(); r = request(); assert r.status == 409 and r.json.error.error_type == 'workspace_busy' and now() - t0 < holdDuration; release(); assert request().status == 200

tests.title: A lock whose holder stops is released
given: a workspace whose lock is taken by a component that is then stopped without releasing it
tests.when: a lock-taking request is made afterwards
then: the request eventually succeeds rather than answering 409 indefinitely
the workspace is usable again without operator intervention
tests.pseudocode: in the workspace lock integration test file: take(lock); kill(holder); assert eventually(lambda: request().status == 200)

tests.title: The lock serialises across instances, not only within one
given: two instances of the service sharing one platform, and one workspace
tests.when: a lock-taking operation is started on the first instance and a second is requested on the other
then: the second answers 409 with error_type workspace_busy while the first holds the lock
it succeeds once the first releases
the same holds with the two instances swapped
tests.pseudocode: in the workspace lock integration test file, with two service instances over one store: assert instanceB.request().status == 409 while instanceA holds

tests.title: Every sandbox route answers sandboxes_disabled before any other check
given: an authenticated caller with no sandbox scope, a workspace, an archived workspace and a slug naming nothing
tests.when: each sandbox path the reference lists is requested, against each of those workspaces
then: every call answers 404 with error_type sandboxes_disabled and the message "sandboxes are not enabled on this hub"
the answer is the same for the missing scope, the archived workspace and the unknown slug
no sandbox path falls through to the router's unmatched-path 404, which carries no error_type
tests.pseudocode: in the sandbox routes' test file, table over (path, workspace) asserting status, error_type and message

tests.title: An unauthenticated sandbox request is refused for the credential, not the provider
given: a service with no sandbox provider
tests.when: each sandbox path is requested with no Authorization header
then: each answers 401 with the message "authentication required"
no response carries error_type sandboxes_disabled
tests.pseudocode: in the sandbox routes' test file, table over the paths asserting 401 and the absence of the sandboxes_disabled type

tests.title: An owner registers a workspace and reads it back against a running deployment
given: a running deployment and a signed-in user with a personal organization
tests.when: a workspace is created with a git URL and a git_pat, then read by slug and found in the list
then: the create answers 201 with status pending and access owner
the read returns the same record with every setting at its effective value
the list contains it
the stored credential is not present in any response
tests.pseudocode: in the workspace smoke test file, against a running deployment: r = post('/api/v1/workspaces', body); assert get(f'/api/v1/workspaces/{slug}').json.slug == slug and slug in slugs(get('/api/v1/workspaces'))

tests.title: A member reads the workspace and is refused a write and a private route
given: a running deployment, a workspace, and a second user who is a member of its organization
tests.when: the member reads the workspace, attempts an update, and lists the workspace's bound tokens
then: the read succeeds with access member and the owner's field values
the update answers 403 with error_type forbidden
the bound token list answers 404 workspace not found
tests.pseudocode: in the workspace smoke test file: assert read(member).json.access == 'member'; assert patch(member).json.error.error_type == 'forbidden'; assert tokens(member).status == 404

tests.title: A bound token reaches its own workspace and nothing else, against a running deployment
given: a running deployment, two workspaces owned by the same user
tests.when: a token bound to the first is minted and then used on the first workspace, on the second, and on POST /api/v1/workspaces
then: the first workspace is served
the second answers 404 workspace not found
the create answers 403 with error_type token_bound and a message naming the bound workspace
tests.pseudocode: in the workspace smoke test file: t = mint_bound(ws1); assert read(ws1, t).status == 200 and read(ws2, t).status == 404 and create(t).json.error.error_type == 'token_bound'

tests.title: A workspace is archived then deleted, and its bound token dies with it
given: a running deployment, a ready workspace with a live bound token
tests.when: the workspace is archived, an update is attempted, the workspace is deleted, and the bound token is used
then: the archive answers 200 with status archived
the update answers 400
the delete answers 204 and the workspace is gone from the list
the bound token is refused 401
tests.pseudocode: in the workspace smoke test file: post(archive); assert patch().status == 400; assert delete().status == 204; assert call(boundToken).status == 401
